How readily to call a meal
100% = as fitted to your data. 200% doubles the odds that a rise is called a meal, 50% halves them.
Carbs of a typical meal. The fit of each rise is pulled toward this size.
How much meal size varies (plus or minus). A larger spread lets the fit follow the data more.
How long the carb effect of a typical meal lasts
How much the rise length varies (plus or minus)
Where the carb effect peaks, as a share of the rise: 0 = at the start, 1 = at the end
How long the carb effect stays above half its peak, as a share of the rise. Smaller = a sharper peak.
After the peak, the carb effect still to come halves every this many minutes

Once an hour, moves the low line a little, from the BG of the last 7 days. In shadow mode the line is not moved, because MPC does not dose and so cannot change that BG. The MPC screen then shows which way it would go.
Off: the low line stays as set
Mean BG of a target HbA1c

The low line moves so that the mean BG of the last 7 days goes toward the mean this HbA1c stands for. It stays between 10 mg/dL below and 25 mg/dL above the low line you set, and never goes down while more than 1% of readings are below 3.9 mmol/L.
Lows you accept per 1% less time high (%)

How much more time below 3.9 mmol/L you accept for each 1% less time above 10 mmol/L. 0.20 means: 1% less time high is worth 0.2% more time low. The rate is measured as time in 3.3 to 4.4 mmol/L against time in 9.4 to 10.6 mmol/L, and the low line moves until it matches your value. It stays between 20 mg/dL below and 30 mg/dL above the low line you set.

0 = off. While BG has stayed within 1.5 mmol/L (27 mg/dL) for 90 min and no meal is seen, both lines go down 9 mg/dL every 30 min, at most by this much. Any change puts them straight back. 27 worked best on the replay.
No MPC run yet. It runs with the loop every 5 minutes.
